newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea orders student arrests after police death.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea orders student arrests after police death.

text.p: A South Korean riot policeman died after fierce clashes on Monday with militant students, the first fatality in four days of violent protests in Seoul to demand the resignation of President Kim Young-sam.
A police official said the 21-year-old officer, Yoo Ji-woong, died in hospital.

Witnesses said a number of police officers were beaten senseless as thousands of students brandishing heavy metal pipes and hurling firebombs burst through a security cordon outside Hanyang University.
The students were trying to join a ceremony on the campus organised by the outlawed leftwing student body, Hanchongryon, to inaugurate new office-holders.
South Korea's chief prosecutor immediately ordered the arrest of "criminals" responsible for the death, signalling that another harsh crackdown on students may be imminent.

An official statement said Kim Ki-soo also instructed authorities to seize top Hanchongryon leaders and punish them severely. The protests were a "violent uprising" that had disrupted life in the capital by halting trains and subways, it added.
Students have been staging hit-and-run raids on police squads posted in downtown areas by cruising the subway system and emerging without warning to hurl rocks and firebombs.

Violence that has left large areas of Seoul strewn with rubble, smashed glass and spent teargas canisters was sparked by President Kim's refusal to bow to opposition demands and reveal how much he spent on his 1992 election.
Allegations that Kim grossly overspent have surfaced in the final year of his presidency in the wake of a corruption scandal involving loans to the Hanbo Group.
The Hanbo scandal has led to the arrest of Kim's second son and shattered his credibility.
Hand-to-hand fighting erupted around a bridge leading to Hanyang University as darkness fell.

Chanting students, some sporting white headbands reading "Kim Young-sam Resign", marched at squadrons of police blocking the bridge. They hurled petrol bombs and lashed out with long iron bars at officers, who defended themselves with shields, clubs and volleys of tear gas.

Bystanders summoned help from a passing driver for the officer as he lay dying, the police official said. Doctors found he had a bloody nose and a bruise under one eye, but no other outward signs of injury.

At the height of Monday's fighting, one student ran screaming from police lines, flames pouring from the back of his shirt that had caught fire. Other students pelted police with rocks from a pedestrian overpass.
Injured officers were sprawled helplessly on the streets, their helmets scattered all around them.
At one point, students disarmed and seized about 10 officers, but by late evening their fate was unclear.
A haze of teargas from shells fired by armoured police vehicles with multiple launchers engulfed the area. Students wore white cotton masks to protect themselves.
Towards midnight, around 10,000 students had gathered inside the college grounds and fighting had ended.
Earlier on Monday, a Seoul court sentenced Hanbo's 74-year-old patriach to 15 years in jail after convicting him of bribing top aides to President Kim, bankers and others.
Chung Tae-soo was one of 10 people handed stiff prison sentences in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal involving Hanbo's failed steelmaking flagship.
The others are a former cabinet minister, three lawmakers with the ruling New Korea Party and one with the main opposition party, three ex-bankers and Chung's son, who is Hanbo's current chairman.
